items.goal: Opening the catalog with a page number past the last page (e.g. /?page=50 with 101 products, 9 per page) shows the last page's products and a pager reading '12 / 12', with or without brand/type filters; valid pages and filters behave as today.
items.verifyReason: Visible pager and product grid behaviour on the catalog page.

alternatives.reason: Extra round trip and redirect handling on static SSR with streaming rendering; the story only requires showing the last page.
API returning a different page than requested changes its contract; the bug is in the WebApp.

follow_ups.title: Catalog API overflows on large pageIndex
follow_ups.reason: CatalogApi.GetAllItems computes Skip(pageSize * pageIndex) in int, so a large pageIndex makes the skip value negative and the request fails instead of returning a validation error.

subject: test-planner
reason: Split by page position (in-range pages 1 and 12, just past at 13, far past at 50, largest int value) and by filter shape (multi-page brand, multi-page full-last-page type, single-page brand, filter matching nothing), all e2e on the WebApp because the defect is in the Blazor page's rendering.

excluded.reason: The story does not say whether the address changes (Open questions)

items.title: The catalog's last page /?page=12 lists 2 products with the pager at "12 / 12"
covers: Expected: pages 1 to 12 behave exactly as today
items.reason: Step 1 of the reproduction is the baseline every past-the-end case compares against, and the ticket requires page 12 (the last valid page, just inside the limit) to behave as today. It must be an e2e case because the rendering of the count, products and pager happens in the Blazor page.

items.title: /?page=1 lists 9 products with the pager at "1 / 12"
covers: Expected: pages 1 to 12 behave exactly as today
items.reason: The fix changes how the page computes the current page; the ticket requires in-range pages to be unchanged. Page 1 is the other end of the valid range, where a wrong clamp (for example to the last page) would show up. E2e because the pager is rendered by the page.

items.title: /?page=50 shows the catalog's last page with the pager at "12 / 12"
covers: Expected bullet 1: step 2 shows the last page
Expected bullet 2: pager never above the number of pages (no filter)
items.reason: This is the reported defect itself: a page number past the end showed "101 products" over an empty product area and a pager reading "50 / 12". E2e reproduces the ticket's exact steps on the test stack.

items.title: /?page=13, one past the last page, shows the last page
covers: Expected bullet 2: pager never above the number of pages (no filter, just outside the limit)
items.reason: Page 13 is the first value just outside the limit; an off-by-one in the comparison with the last page would leave it empty while 50 works. E2e for the same reason as TC-BUG-51-03.

items.title: /?page=2147483647 shows the last page
covers: Expected bullet 2: pager never shows a current page larger than the number of pages (largest page value)
items.reason: "Never" in the ticket includes the largest page number the page accepts. The paging offset (page − 1) × 9 does not fit in an int for this value, so a naive request could fail instead of showing the last page. E2e because the value travels from the address through the WebApp to the Catalog API.

items.title: A brand filter past its last page shows that filter's last page
covers: Expected bullet 2: with a brand filter
Expected bullet 3: brand-filtered catalog behaves as today
items.reason: The ticket says the pager must stay in range "with or without a brand or type filter", so the last page must be computed from the filtered count (2 pages), not the whole catalog's (12). Step 1 also pins the filtered in-range page as unchanged. E2e because the filter and page come from the address.

items.title: A type filter past its last page shows that filter's last page
covers: Expected bullet 2: with a type filter
Expected bullet 3: type-filtered catalog behaves as today
items.reason: The ticket names the type filter separately from the brand filter; it is a separate query value and needs its own case. Type 3 has exactly 18 products, so its last page is full, which also checks the last-page computation when the count is an exact multiple of 9.

items.title: A one-page brand filter with a page past the end shows its products and no pager
covers: Expected bullet 2: pager never above the number of pages (filter with a single page)
items.reason: When the filtered result fits on one page, the last page is page 1 and the page shows no pager today. Without the fix, a page past the end would show the count above an empty area; this is the smallest non-empty last page.

items.title: A filter matching nothing with a page past the end keeps the no-products state
covers: Expected bullet 3: filtered catalog behaves exactly as today (no matching products)
items.reason: A filter that matches nothing has zero pages; the fix must not turn that into a page 0 or a count above an empty grid. The ticket requires the filtered catalog to behave as today, and today it shows the no-products state.
